To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the local gene regulation at the primary lesion site is different in optic nerve and sciatic nerve crush lesions.
differential gene regulation in the crush lesions of the rat optic and sciatic nerve was observed, with the optic nerve showing more downregulation and the sciatic nerve more upregulation.
the differential gene regulation in optic and sciatic nerve crush lesions is reflected by different cell types, signaling, metabolism, translation and transcription, and by different proteases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential regulation of genes after nerve injury.
the question of whether the molecular events that occur at the lesion site are similar in the two types of nerve.
differential regulation in crush lesions of the rat ON and SN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ON lesion and the SN lesion have a lot in common and that the differences in the regulation of genes are more important for the regeneration of the ON than for the SN.
the differential gene regulation in ON vs. SN lesions is not a result of a different injury but rather a result of a difference in the local environment of the lesion.
the local response to crush lesion is very different in the central versus the peripheral nervous system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are many differences between CNS and PNS crush lesions, and that the CNS crush lesion is more similar to a PNS transection.
the central nervous system lesion site is a complex environment that is different from the peripheral nervous system lesion site.
in central and peripheral nervous systems the local reaction after injury differs in many respects and that this is likely to be of importance for the regeneration process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the differential orchestration of gene regulation has implications to axonal regeneration in CNS lesions.
the differential gene expression pattern in crush lesions of the rat optic nerve and sciatic nerve is relevant to the different capacity of these two nerve types to regenerate.
gene regulation in the lesion site is different between the central and peripheral nervous systems.
